subject: math

objective.text: Use the fewest number of coins to make a given value.

explanations.title: Fewest coins
explanations.text: It is easier to carry fewer coins. To use the fewest coins, use the coins with the greatest value.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (S: use coins with the greatest possible value)

explanations.title: Trade for a bigger coin
explanations.text: Trade small coins for one coin of greater value. 2 dimes and 1 nickel trade for 1 quarter. 4 nickels trade for 2 dimes. You now have fewer coins.

explanations.title: Break the total into coin values
explanations.text: Break the total into as many twenty-fives as you can. Then tens. Then fives. Use pennies for what is left.

explanations.title: Tips for fewer coins
explanations.text: Do not use pennies if you can use a bigger coin. Use a dime instead of 2 nickels. Try a quarter because it is worth the most.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (S: I didn't use pennies; a dime instead of 2 nickels; a quarter is worth the most)

examples.title: 40 cents
examples.text: 40 cents is 4 dimes. It is also 1 quarter and 3 nickels. Or 1 quarter, 1 dime and 1 nickel. The last way uses the fewest coins, 3.

examples.title: 35 cents: trade coins
examples.text: 3 dimes and 1 nickel is 4 coins. Trade 2 dimes and 1 nickel for 1 quarter. Now you have 1 quarter and 1 dime. That is 2 coins.

examples.title: 60 cents: trade coins
examples.text: 4 dimes and 4 nickels is 8 coins. Trade 4 dimes and 2 nickels for 2 quarters. Now you have 2 quarters and 1 dime. That is 3 coins.

examples.title: 27 cents
examples.text: 27 is 25 and 2 more. Use 1 quarter and 2 pennies. That is the fewest coins.

assets_required.why_this_method: Exact coin counts and coin images need exact behaviour. Diffusion cannot count or draw the same coin every time.
assets_required.description: Coins in groups on mats. Each coin is a penny, nickel, dime or quarter. The child can trade coins for coins of the same value and the widget shows how many coins are on the mat.
must_show_exactly: Exactly the coins in the stimulus
Each coin looks like its real coin
Coins can be moved and traded
A coin count is shown only when the stimulus asks
Trades keep the total value the same

4 dimes and 4 nickels traded to 2 quarters and 1 dime
Fewest coins for 43, 56, 80 cents and 1 dollar
assets_required.interaction: Tutor sets the coins from the stimulus. Child can move or trade coins. Child answers by voice or typing.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
